      "title": "Scaling up Ranking under Constraints for Live Recommendations by Replacing Optimization with Prediction",
      "research_question": "Can constrained personalized ranking be made fast enough for live recommendation by predicting per-user optimization shadow prices instead of solving the full constrained optimization problem online?",
      "methodology": "The authors reformulate constrained ranking through the dual of a weighted bipartite matching problem and solve for optimal constraint shadow prices offline on sampled users. They train a k-nearest-neighbor model to predict those shadow prices from user covariates at serving time, then recover rankings using the adjusted utility scores. Experiments use MovieLens 25M and YOW News with five and eight constraints respectively, comparing no optimization, per-user optimal optimization, mean shadow prices, and personalized predicted shadow prices. Evaluation measures constraint compliance, achieved utility, and computation time for ranking 50, 500, or 1,000 items.",

        {
          "finding": "Predicting personalized shadow prices substantially reduces online computation while retaining constraint compliance close to the per-user optimization solution.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The KNeighbors shadow-price approach stays within the paper's 50 millisecond serving-time requirement even when ranking 1,000 items subject to at least five constraints.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "A single mean shadow-price vector performs worse than personalized shadow-price prediction on MovieLens, providing evidence that modeling user heterogeneity can improve constraint compliance.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "On YOW News, personalized and mean shadow-price prediction have similar constraint-compliance performance, so the benefit of personalization is dataset-dependent.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Ignoring optimization produces the worst constraint compliance, whereas utility differences among constrained methods are generally small.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The framework explicitly separates a primary utility objective from auxiliary requirements expressed as hard ranking constraints, making it relevant to obligation-versus-preference prioritization even though it does not model workplace obligations.",

          "section": "2.2 Adding constraints and 4.2 Evaluation"
        }

        "Reported online runtimes exclude data generation, reading, preprocessing, and offline computation, so they are serving-stage rather than end-to-end latency measurements.",
        "The prediction approach assumes useful user covariates are available and that offline shadow-price relationships generalize to future users.",

Uncertainty is encoded through graphical features including line thickness, semi-transparent positional circles, and a track-quality value.       "paper_id": "doi-10-1145-2523813",
      "title": "A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation",
      "research_question": "How can online supervised learning systems characterize, detect, adapt to, and evaluate changes in the relationship between inputs and targets over evolving data streams?",
      "methodology": "This is a comprehensive survey rather than a new controlled experiment. It organizes concept-drift research into an adaptive-learning framework containing memory, change detection, learning, and loss-estimation components, and reviews representative algorithms within those categories. It also analyzes forgetting strategies, fixed and variable windows, explicit drift detectors, adaptation mechanisms, and evaluation procedures for time-ordered data. The survey discusses application examples and proposes evaluation criteria for both predictive performance and change-detection quality.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Concept drift includes changes in the target distribution conditional on observed inputs, and changing user interests in a news stream are presented as a canonical example.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2.1 Setting and definitions"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Adaptive learning can be decomposed into memory, change detection, learning, and loss-estimation modules, allowing different adaptation strategies to be combined modularly.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "2.4 and 3 Taxonomy"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Shorter recent-data windows react faster to changes but can be less stable, whereas larger windows improve stability in stationary periods while adapting more slowly.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.1 Memory"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Recency alone is not a reliable proxy for relevance when data are noisy or concepts recur, so simple window-based forgetting can discard useful older information.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.1 Memory"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Explicit change detection provides information about when and how a process changes beyond the implicit adaptation obtained from continuously updating an online model.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.2 Change Detection"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Drift detectors should be evaluated not only by downstream predictive accuracy but also by true-change detection, false alarms, detection delay, and change-point localization accuracy.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.1 Performance evaluation metrics"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Ordinary randomized cross-validation is inappropriate for evolving streams because it destroys temporal order; holdout and prequential test-then-train procedures are presented as alternatives.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.2 Experimental design"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The survey focuses primarily on online supervised learning where labels or delayed feedback are available, not on unsupervised semantic state tracking in workplace communication.",
        "As a 2014 survey, it cannot cover later developments in drift detection, continual learning, modern recommender systems, or language-model-based personalization.",
        "The work synthesizes heterogeneous prior algorithms rather than conducting a uniform empirical benchmark across all reviewed methods.",
        "Many drift-handling techniques assume a stream of labeled instances and do not directly specify symbolic work-item transitions such as new, open, resolved, or superseded.",
        "The survey does not address briefing-specific omission, repetition, evidence attribution, or obligation-versus-preference ranking."

    {
      "paper_id": "doi-10-1155-2016-1340973",
      "title": "Mining Sequential Update Summarization with Hierarchical Text Analysis",
      "research_question": "Can a hierarchical combination of time-sensitive retrieval, topic-level keyword mining, and sentence scoring produce useful, novel, timely, and sufficiently comprehensive updates for rapidly developing events?",
      "methodology": "The system processes a time-ordered document stream using three stages: event-relevant retrieval with Indri, hierarchical LDA for time-dependent keyword extraction, and one of three sentence-scoring methods called KLP, SKD, and KS. Exact duplicate sentences are removed, with the earliest occurrence retained. The authors evaluate on ten TREC 2013 Temporal Summarization events drawn from a timestamped corpus of more than one billion documents, selecting the top 60 updates per topic. Updates are matched to human-created gold nuggets and scored using expected gain, expected latency gain, comprehensiveness, and latency comprehensiveness.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The system explicitly treats novelty and timeliness as first-class properties of sequential updates and suppresses duplicate sentences before submission.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3 Sentence Scoring Module"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Evaluation separates a precision-like notion of useful nonredundant information from a recall-like notion of nugget coverage, with latency-sensitive variants of both.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5 Evaluation Method"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The KS scorer reaches expected gain 0.149 and expected latency gain 0.136, equal to the best reported values shown in the paper's TREC comparison table.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6.2 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "KLP provides substantially higher comprehensiveness than KS, while KS provides substantially higher expected gain, demonstrating a direct accuracy-versus-coverage tradeoff.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6.2 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Within KLP variants, changing sentence-length and position weights has little effect compared with keyword diversity, which the authors identify as the more influential feature.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "6.2 Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The paper's prose claims that all three investigated methods are above the reported midvalue for comprehensiveness, but Table 3 shows SKD at 0.131 and KS at 0.099 versus a midvalue of 0.204, while one KLP variant merely equals 0.204.",
          "evidence_type": "contradicted",
          "section": "6.2 Results, Table 3 versus accompanying text"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The evaluation jointly exposes omission and repetition-related concerns through nugget coverage, expected gain, latency penalties, verbosity penalties, and duplicate removal, but it does not combine them into an explicit longitudinal work-item state-transition metric.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.3, 5, and 6"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "Evaluation uses only ten unexpected-news events from the TREC 2013 Temporal Summarization task.",

        "The system is not personalized to individual recipients and does not distinguish mandatory obligations from preferences.",
        "Only the top 60 candidate updates per topic are assessed, so behavior deeper in the ranked stream is not evaluated.",
        "The paper contains an internal inconsistency between the prose interpretation and the numerical comprehensiveness results in Table 3."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "novel_timely_updates": 0.99,

        "The task is to emit sentence-length updates from a temporally ordered document stream as an event develops.",
        "The system combines time-sensitive retrieval, hierarchical topic analysis, and sentence scoring.",
        "Hierarchical LDA is used to obtain event-relevant keywords.",
        "Three update scorers named KLP, SKD, and KS are evaluated.",

      "access": "full_text",
      "source_citation": "citeturn366749view2turn335599view0turn335599view1"

      "paper_id": "doi-10-1109-fuzz-ieee-2016-7737835",
      "title": "Fuzzy user-interest drift detection based recommender systems",
      "research_question": "Can fuzzy modeling of individual user-interest consistency combined with concept-drift detection improve recommendation accuracy when user interests evolve and item-interest information is incomplete or vague?",
      "methodology": "The authors construct a fuzzy user-interest consistency model using fuzzy-set theory and develop a user-interest drift-detection mechanism based on concept-drift techniques.
